chunks: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani al-Mukattib (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa b. Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid from Ali b. Salim from his father. He said:

I visited al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them) in Rajab when it still had a few days left. When he looked at me, he said to me: O Salim! Have you fasted at all this month? I said: No, by Allah, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said to me: You have indeed missed out on a reward whose extent is known only to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Surely, this is a month that Allah gave virtue to, magnified its sanctity, and made His blessing incumbent upon those who fast in it.

He said: So I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, if I fast something of what remains of it, will I attain some of the reward of those who have fasted in it? So he said: O Salim! Whoever fasts one day at the end of this month, that will be a source of safety for him from the severity of the pangs of death, and a source of safety for him from the horror of the resurrection and the punishment of the grave. Whoever fasts two days at the end of this month, he will thereby have safe passage upon the Path. Whoever fasts three days at the end of this month will be safe on the Day of the Greatest Dismay from its horrors and its severities, and will be given a release from the Fire.

key_terms.الصراط: The Bridge over Hellfire that all must cross on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الفزع الأكبر: The Greatest Dismay, referring to the terrors of the Day of Judgment
key_terms.رجب: Rajab, the seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar and one of the four sacred months
key_terms.سكرات الموت: The pangs or agonies of death experienced at the moment of dying
key_terms.هول المطلع: The horror of the place of beholding, referring to what one encounters after death

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of fasting in the month of Rajab according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq explains to his companion Salim the immense rewards of fasting in the month of Rajab, one of the four sacred months in Islam. The Imam describes escalating rewards for fasting one, two, or three days at the end of Rajab: safety from the pangs of death, safe passage on the Bridge (Sirat), and protection from the horrors of the Day of Judgment along with freedom from Hellfire.
